授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: This course will introduce you to four different issues which are, or are becoming, controversial in Japan today, and which are often thought to be a special problem because people assume there is a "perception gap" (認識の違い) between how Japanese and western people understand them. These issues are whaling, cultural appropriation, hate speech and the morality of the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. During this course you will read, think about, discuss and write about these issues, and ask yourselves how deep those perception gaps are, and whether those gaps are only between different "cultures".

事前/事後学修の内容
rows: This section explores different understandings of the whaling controversy in Japan, including whalers, Japanese government, media, animal rights activists and environmentalists

In this section very different responses to the issue of cultural appropriation and Japanese traditional fashion will be considered, looking at the opinions of anti-racism activists, journalists, academics and fashion experts
In this section we consider how hate speech has been understood in a Japanese context by different groups, including Zainichi activists, foreign journalists and academics.
The justification for the atomic bombings

In the final part of the course we will discuss one of the oldest and most famous perception gaps relating to Japanese history - whether or not it was justified to use the atomic bombs against Hiroshima and Nagasaki to end World War II. We will explore the different opinions of Japanese and American historians, philosophers and politicians.
